title: Undo UX: Designing for Reversibility
summary: This lesson explains why providing an 'Undo' option is superior to 'Are you sure?' confirmation dialogs for most user actions. It covers soft deletes, matching friction to the cost of irreversible actions, and using grace periods to prevent common mistakes.

transcript.text: Are you sure punishes everyone for one person's mistake.
Undo punishes nobody. The action happens instantly, and regret gets a second chance.
The file left your screen, not the database. A deleted flag, 30 days in trash, then it's gone for real. Deletion is a state, not an event.
Some actions have no way back. That's where friction belongs. GitHub makes you type the repo name before it deletes. Earn the irreversible.
One undo is a toast. A stack is a time machine. Command-Z walks back through every step in order. Figma remembers everything you did. Your app can too.
Gmail holds your email for 10 seconds after send. The delay is the feature. You catch the typo, the wrong recipient, the reply-all disaster.
Design for regret. Follow for more UX patterns. Save this before you delete something.
